Use case: scientific-educational.
Asset type: a new landscape explanatory bitmap for a Chinese robotics technical blog, roughly 16:9.
Primary request: visually distinguish path time parameterization (TOPP-RA) from state-to-state jerk-limited trajectory generation (Ruckig).
Style reference description: match the existing Transformer teaching illustrations: pure white background, very pale blue and green rounded panels, restrained lavender and amber highlights, thin crisp colored outlines, dark navy sans-serif labels, clear arrows, ample whitespace, flat vector-like scientific illustration. No photographic elements, no decorative robots, no watermark.
Composition: two equal panels side by side under title "Two Different Trajectory Problems".
Left blue panel heading "TOPP-RA". Three stacked stages connected downward: "Given path q(s)" with a small 2D joint-space curved path, then "Solve timing s(t)" with a monotone smooth time curve, then "Trajectory q(s(t))" with the SAME joint-space curve and nonuniform sample dots. Small footer "Keep the geometric path". The same curve must remain identical before and after timing. Label miniature joint-space axes q1 and q2, time axes t and s.
Right green panel heading "Ruckig". At top two compact boxes side by side labeled "Current state" and "Target state", each contains "position, velocity, acceleration". Both feed a center box "Velocity / acceleration / jerk limits", then downward into box "Generate q(t)" with simple smooth position profiles versus t for two joints, then footer "State-to-state; no prescribed path".
Bottom shared note "Neither example checks collisions".
Constraints: exact English labels only, no numeric measurements or fabricated data, no claims that TOPP-RA adds jerk constraints, no claims that Ruckig preserves a pre-existing path; curves are conceptual and not measured plots. All arrows unambiguous and no overlaps. Readable large type with generous margins.
images.revision_prompt: Edit only the two green miniature q1(t) and q2(t) plots in the Ruckig right panel. Preserve every label, text, arrow, all left TOPP-RA content, colors, borders, layout, and white background. Make q1 a smooth monotonic increasing S curve from a lower initial plateau to a distinctly higher final plateau. Make q2 a smooth monotonic decreasing S curve from a higher initial plateau to a distinctly lower final plateau. No humps, excursions or reversal in either curve; both show different initial and final positions with horizontal endpoint tangents. These are conceptual position profiles, not measured results. No other changes.
